chunks: And in it is that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say in his supplication: O Allah, I ask You by Your Greatest Name, which when called upon is answered, and when asked for is given.

O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which You placed in Your Book, made a witness among Your creation with it, derived it from Your Knowledge, entrusted it to Your Book, preserved it on the tongue of Your Prophet, sent it down through the hand of Your Messenger, revealed it in the Preserved Tablet, and made it known in the Guarded Tablet.

O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which I make the sky with its height, the clouds with their covering, the sea with its might, the fire with its flame, the power with its strength, the wind with its blowing, the sun with its radiance, the moon with its light, the night with its darkness, the day with its joy, the dawn with its concealment, the morning with its clarity, the shadows with their hiding, the mountains with their elevation, the earth with its expanse, the sky with its peaks, the earth with its foundation, the angels with their number, the Spirit with its power, the soul with its contentment, the heart with its connection, the tongue with its speech, the eye with its light, the ear with its hearing, the hand with its grasping, the foot with its walking, the head with its knowledge, the body with its structure, the Throne with its majesty, the Footstool with its bounty, the House with its sanctity, the Prophet with his mission, the Imam with his guardianship, the Witness with his presence, the Witnessed with his occultation, the Truth with its certainty, the creation with its need, the Creator with His wealth, the Living with His self-subsistence, the Eternal with His eternity, the Everlasting with His permanence, the First with His beginning, the Last with His end, the Apparent with His manifestation, the Hidden with His concealment, the One with His uniqueness, the Single with His oneness, the Sufficient with His decree, the Desired with His desirability.

O Allah, I ask You by Your Name which when called upon opens the doors of mercy, when asked for gives to the petitioner, when witnessed testifies to the truth, when summoned invites to good, when sent down brings mercy, when preserved protects from His affair, when witnessed testifies to the truth, when revealed conveys wisdom, when clarified clarifies with speech, when revealed shows majesty, when made known knows the unseen.

So by Your Name I ask You, O Lord, to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to bestow upon us from Your bounty, and to give us from Your gift, and to answer our supplication, and to fulfill our need, and to enrich us from Your grace, and to provide for us from Your sustenance, and to guide us from Your guidance, and to rectify our affair, and to rectify for us our religion and our world and our Hereafter, and to make us among the righteous.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of Imam Ali regarding the Greatest Name of Allah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Kamal al-Din*, this supplication highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the *Ism Allah al-A'zam* as a conduit for divine grace, reflecting the belief that Allah’s knowledge encompasses all things (as noted in the opening verse). The enumeration of creation’s attributes serves not merely as praise but as a means of aligning the supplicant’s heart with the Divine Will, a practice central to Shia devotional literature for seeking intercession and fulfillment of needs.
